MAS.thesis_one_line: A cash-generative faucets-and-cabinets maker trading cheaply while U.S. home-repair spending stays weak, propped up this quarter by a one-time tariff refund.
kill_criteria: Organic net sales growth negative year-over-year for three consecutive quarters (already 2 of the last 3: Q4'25 -2%, Q2'26 -2.9%).
TTM operating cash flow declines for a fourth consecutive fiscal year (would mean FY2026 OCF below ~$1,000M).
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut from the current $4.40-$4.60.
Incremental China-tariff exposure escalates materially above the ~$625-675M scenario management has already flagged.
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 revenue -3%, operating profit -8%; operating cash flow down for a third straight year (FY2023 $1,413M -> FY2024 $1,075M -> FY2025 $1,022M, -27.7% cumulative).
GAAP net income has declined in each of the last two fiscal years (FY2023 $908M -> FY2024 $822M -> FY2025 $810M) even as EPS has been supported by a 13.4% share-count reduction since mid-2022.

The Q2 2026 guidance raise (to $4.40-$4.60 adjusted EPS) is substantially explained by a one-time $95M net IEEPA tariff refund, not a demand recovery; FY2026 sales guidance remains only 'low single digits'.
Stockholders' equity is negative (-$242M at Q1 2026) and long-term debt has been flat at $2,945M for years with no deleveraging.
Direct China tariff exposure is material: ~$450M of sourced goods, with a management-cited scenario implying up to ~$625M of annualised incremental exposure in a worst case.
data_conflicts: Q2 2026 (period ended 2026-06-30) balance-sheet XBRL data was not yet available in SEC's bulk companyfacts API at time of review; balance-sheet figures used are as of Q1 2026 (2026-03-31) while income-statement figures for Q2 2026 are sourced directly from the 8-K earnings release. Not a substantive conflict, but a recency gap to disclose.
MAS.confidence_in_thesis: medium (the multi-year OCF and operating-profit deterioration is clearly evidenced across primary filings, but two more quarters are needed to confirm whether repair/remodel demand has troughed or is still declining)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's near-neutral 'fair' verdict and near-zero implied growth (+0.44%/yr over 10 years) are consistent with what MAS has actually delivered (5-year CAGR -0.8%, OCF down 3 straight years); I do not see a valuation mispricing here in either direction, only a fairly-priced, currently-deteriorating business whose Q2 2026 guidance raise is largely a one-off tariff refund rather than a fundamental inflection.

VRSN.thesis_one_line: The sole gatekeeper for .com and .net web addresses, raising prices every year and buying back stock, priced for more growth than history supports.
kill_criteria: ICANN/.com pricing authority is capped, revoked or renegotiated below the current '7%/yr in years 3-6' framework before the Nov 2030 expiry.
Domain-base growth falls back below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters (current guide 5.2%-6.0%).
Quarterly revenue growth decelerates below 4% YoY for two consecutive quarters (currently +6.0% Q2'26, +6.6% Q1'26).
A materially adverse outcome in any future .com/.net registry-agreement renewal or a DOJ/ICANN antitrust or regulatory action against the arrangement.
Added by RA14: the FY2027 revenue growth guide comes in below 8% (the announced .com +6.9% from 1 Nov 2026, .net +10% from 1 Mar 2027 and domain-base growth of about 5% should deliver about 9-10%)
key_adverse_facts: V1's reverse-DCF implies the current 27.3x NTM P/E is pricing in ~14.5%/yr growth for a decade, well above the delivered 5-year CAGR of 5.8% and 10-year CAGR of 4.4%.
The peer set used for relative valuation (AKAM, GDDY) is thin (2 names) and an imperfect business-model match for a sole-source registry monopoly.
Stockholders' equity is negative and deepening (-$2,254.1M at Q2 2026, from -$1,977.0M at Q1 2025); buybacks have exceeded net income in most recent years (FY2025 107% of NI, FY2024 156% of NI).
A new $550M 5.10% senior notes issuance (June 2026, redeeming $550M 4.75% notes due 2027) modestly raises the cost of debt.
H1 2026 operating cash flow growth (+2.1% YoY) decelerated sharply from the FY2025 pace (+20.9% YoY) - direction not yet clear (timing/working-capital vs. genuine moderation).

Base-path value is about $272 versus $287.25 (-5%) and the probability-weighted three-year return is about +4.8% a year, so there is no valuation cushion; the 30 Nov 2030 .com expiry falls inside the ten-year growth the price requires.
data_conflicts: V1 flagged VRSN's ~68% TTM EBIT margin as 'implausible' and substituted an alternate revenue source for its reverse-DCF; this review independently confirms via primary SEC filings and the Q2 2026 earnings release (68.2% GAAP operating margin) that the margin is real and structural to the registry business, not a data error. V1's conflict flag appears to be a false positive, though it does not appear to have materially changed V1's output values.

The Q2 2026 guidance figures in the dossier (revenue $1.745-1.755B, operating income $1.185-1.195B, domain-base growth 5.2-6.0%) are not in any SEC filing: the filed Q2 release says only that guidance was raised; the Q1 slide figures were confirmed on the investor site. V1's 14.5% 'implied growth' is the year-1 rate of a ten-year fade to 3% (constant-growth equivalent 9.5% at a 9.24% WACC), so it should not be compared with delivered CAGRs.
VRSN.confidence_in_thesis: medium (business durability and pricing power are high-confidence, primary-source-verified facts; the valuation call - fair, not cheap - is a medium-confidence judgment given the thin peer set and the gap between implied and delivered growth)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I agree with V1's 'fair' verdict and do not dispute the +7.8%/yr base case. I would only soften the 'implied 14.5%/yr growth' framing: exercised pricing power (+7%/yr in years 3-6 of each ICANN cycle, just taken) combined with 5-6% domain-base growth and buyback-driven share shrinkage can plausibly support low-to-mid-teens EPS growth in good years, which is closer to (if still short of) the reverse-DCF's implied rate than a naive read suggests. The +25.8%/yr bull case, requiring a 34.9x exit multiple, is the scenario I would treat with the most scepticism. RESTATED 6 Oct 2026 (RA14): on FCFF after SBC ($1,050M) and EV $27.47B, with a 5.17% Treasury (cost of equity 9.6%, WACC about 9.24%), the price implies 9.5% constant FCF growth for ten years (8.9% at 9.0%, 10.3% at 9.6%); V1's 14.5% was a fade-start rate. The evidence-based base (revenue +9.7% in FY2027 from .com +6.9% and .net +10% steps, about +9% a year to FY2029 while .com steps remain, shares -3.5% a year) gives a path of +12% / +11% / +10% / +9% / +8.5% / +8% / +7% / +6% / +5% / +4% then 3%, returning 8.9% against 9.24% (value about $272, -5%); implied_vs_base is in_line with no cushion. The quarterly dividend ($0.81) is real and V1's $9.58 of cumulative dividends is valid. V1's arithmetic reproduces but used 4.9% revenue growth and a 28.8x exit P/E; restated returns -7.1% / +6.5% / +16.1% a year (probability-weighted +4.8%).

VRSN.scenario_basis: 3-year (to Sep 2029) annualised from $287.25, own arithmetic: diluted EPS FY2026 $9.60; base FY2027-29 $10.86 / $12.05 / $13.26 (+13.1% / +11% / +10%: .com +6.9% from 1 Nov 2026, .net +10% from 1 Mar 2027, domain base +5%, shares -3.5% a year), trailing EPS at Sep 2029 $12.96, exit 26x trailing (31x today), dividends $10.20 ($3.24 a year growing 5%); bear EPS growth +8% / +4% / +3% and 20x; bull +16% / +15% / +14% and 31x. Weights 30/45/25 give +4.8%. Replaces V1 (-10.2% / +7.8% / +25.8%), which reproduces arithmetically but used 4.9% revenue growth and a 28.8x exit multiple.

BKNG.thesis_one_line: The world's largest online travel agent, cheaper than almost any point in its history, buying back massive amounts of stock while EU regulators circle.
kill_criteria: Room-night or gross-bookings growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters (currently +5% / +9%).
Gross debt / TTM adjusted EBITDA rises above 2.5x (currently 1.95x); restated by RA10 2026-10-06 because net debt nets $10.1bn of customer funds against debt.
FY2026 guidance (high-single-digit volume/bookings/revenue, low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth) is cut.
The European Commission opens a formal DMA non-compliance proceeding against Booking.com, or the EU hotel class action produces a disclosed material damages award/settlement.
Quarterly buyback spend falls by more than 50% quarter-over-quarter without a stated capital-return-policy reason.
key_adverse_facts: V1's +39.3%/yr base-case 3-year return depends on the NTM P/E more than doubling (13.8x to 30.1x); management's own FY2026 guidance (low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth) does not support this without substantial multiple re-rating, and the model's base-case fair value already exceeds the Street's highest 12-month price target by 47%.

Shareholders' equity is deeply negative: -$10,783M at Q2 2026, a $4.13bn deterioration over four quarters ($4.67bn over five), funded partly by ~$2.975bn of new debt raised in H1 2026 (total debt +9.2% YoY); H1 2026 buybacks $7.8bn exceed free cash flow ($6.75bn). Corrected by RA10 2026-10-06.

GAAP net income fell sharply YoY in Q1 2025 (-57%) and Q2 2025 (-41%); RA10 resolved the driver: non-cash Euro-debt FX remeasurement losses ($1,350m in H1 2025), convertible-note items and interest expense. 2026 GAAP growth rates are base effects; adjusted EPS (+15% in Q2 2026) is the right comparison.

Booking.com was designated an EU Digital Markets Act 'gatekeeper' (obligations effective Nov 2024); as of April 2026 the European Parliament has pushed for a formal Commission non-compliance investigation over parity clauses, Italy's AGCM opened a related probe, and a hotel-industry class action (potentially ~18,000 European hotels) seeks damages for 2004-2024 conduct.
The GICS peer set used for relative valuation (incl. cruise operator CCL) is an imperfect business-model match.
Bookings growth is decelerating: Q3 2026 guide room nights +3-5%, gross bookings +4-6%; Q2 flights +3.7% (Q1 +28.5%), rental car days -6.5%, gross bookings +9.0% (Q1 +15.2%).
data_conflicts: RESOLVED by RA10 2026-10-06: the GAAP net income vs operating income divergence in Q1-Q2 2025 is non-cash Euro-debt FX remeasurement ($961m loss in Q2 2025), convertible-note amortization ($523m) and fair-value changes, per the Q2 2026 release reconciliation.

All EPS/share-count figures required manual restatement for the April 2026 25-for-1 stock split, since SEC XBRL only retroactively restates comparative periods shown within post-split filings; older discrete quarters (e.g. Q3 2025 as originally tagged) remain on a pre-split basis in the raw data and were divided by 25 for this dossier.
BKNG.confidence_in_thesis: medium (statistical cheapness and low cash-basis leverage are verified; the GAAP earnings-quality question is resolved as non-cash FX, but bookings growth is decelerating, buybacks exceed free cash flow and the EU regulatory/litigation tail risk is unquantified) - RA10 2026-10-06

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I agree with V1's directional 'attractive' verdict (13.8x NTM P/E is genuinely near the 1st percentile of BKNG's own ~15-year history, and operating income has grown every comparable quarter for 4 years) but I do not accept +39.3%/yr as a realistic base case. That figure requires the exit multiple to expand from 13.8x to 30.1x, an assumption not supported by management's own low-to-mid-teens adjusted-EPS guidance or by the Street's highest 12-month price target ($301, 47% below V1's base-case fair value). I would reframe V1's 'base' as this model's bull case and underwrite a realistic base nearer high-teens-to-low-20s%/yr. RA10 2026-10-06: corrected inputs (COE 10.6%, FCF less SBC $8.9bn, working-capital-normalised $7.6bn) imply 2.7-5.0% aggregate growth against an 8% base; base 3-year return +13.4% a year (EPS +12%, exit 14x), not the dossier high-teens-to-low-20s figure.
